item.title: Zelensky says Ukraine ready to de-escalate if Russia halts strikes
item.description:
Ukraine is ready to halt attacks on Russian energy infrastructure if Moscow does the same, President Volodymyr Zelensky said Monday, after US President Donald Trump announced an apparent agreement between the two sides. Kyiv also warned that intensifying Russian strikes on Ukraine’s rail network are worsening each week.

item.title: Rep. Jasmine Crockett’s praise of Chris Brown hit a nerve
item.description:
What happened: Rep. Jasmine Crockett, a Texas Democrat, took the stage in Arlington, Texas, on Saturday to honor R&B singer Chris Brown, delivering official congressional remarks highlighting his career. (She also honored Usher, but people are generally not mad about that.) “Right now, we are experiencing Black joy to the highest level,” Crockett said, according to video of the event. “And I wanted to make sure we document that in the Congressional Record.” Why are people mad: Brown pleaded guilty to felony assault of then-girlfriend Rihanna in 2009. Rihanna was hospitalized after injuries she sustained in the altercation, and a judge issued a restraining order. It’s probably the most well-known incidence of violence in his career but far from the only one. Brown was involved in a January 2013 altercation with singer Frank Ocean. item.title: Africa's richest man launches continent's biggest share sale
item.description:
The News Africa’s richest man Aliko Dangote tapped the opening gong this morning on the floor of the Lagos exchange to open Africa’s largest initial public offer. The $20 billion Dangote Refinery built on swamp land on the outskirts of Lagos becomes the fourth Dangote Industries subsidiary to go public in Nigeria. When the initial offer closes next month, the company will have raised more than $4 billion at about a $50 billion valuation, if demand matches the year-long buzz partly driven by the company’s pledge to pay dividends in US dollars. The refinery will likely account for up to 40% of the Lagos exchange’s capitalization when its shares start trading post IPO in November. “We are going to fully, fully share all our prosperity with the people,” Dangote, 69, said in a packed and celebratory hall of bankers, investors and stock brokers for whom the multibillion-dollar Dangote…

item.title: Texas governor threatens to penalize datacenters not obeying water laws
item.description:
Republican Greg Abbott says datacenters must help ‘protect’ drought-prone state and disclose water use Greg Abbott , the Texas governor, has directed state regulators to penalize datacenters that fail to comply with state laws requiring them to disclose their water use. “Data centers must share the duty to protect Texas water,” the Republican governor said on Monday. “The Texas Water Code requires a complete and accurate water use survey. I direct the Texas Water Development Board to use its enforcement authority to penalize past failures and to impose legal consequences for any future failure to comply,” he added. Continue reading...

Sources: Texas Tribune, The Guardian

item.title: Rights group accuses Israel of dismantling 'Palestinian existence' in West Bank
item.description:
Israeli rights group B'Tselem said Monday that Israeli actions in the occupied West Bank form part of a greater project designed to make it impossible for Palestinians to exist together as a people. In a report titled "The Elimination Project", the group alleged five connected Israeli tactics and policies in the West Bank: "violence, ethnic cleansing, movement restrictions, economic strangulation, social and political destruction". FRANCE 24's Selina Sykes reports.

Covered by 1 nonprofit, 1 public.
Sources: France 24, NPR

item.title: Israel probing Naza film on Gaza for treason, inciting anti-Semitism
item.description:
Miki Zohar accuses Oscar-winning directors Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor of ‘treason against the state’ ‘They know the house they are bombing is full of children’: NAZA’s directors on their devastating film about Israeli intelligence Israel’s culture minister has called for the Oscar-winning Israeli directors of NAZA , a documentary about the country’s mass killing of civilians in Gaza, to be stripped of their citizenship, accusing them of “treason against the state”. NAZA, which was produced by the Guardian, is named for an acronym used by Israel’s intelligence service to indicate how many civilians it expects to die in an airstrike on Gaza. Continue reading...

item.title: Manchester derby VAR officials stood down from weekend Premier League games
item.description:
The Video Assistant Referee is supposed to get everything right. This is an incredibly high standard to hold any sort of officiating, but this is VAR's main selling point and raison d'être . All of the delays, ticky-tack calls, and general disruption to the flow of a soccer match are supposed to be worth it; after all, who doesn't want the correct call made when an incorrect call could decide a match, a season, a legacy? But of course, VAR is not perfect, and it will never be perfect, even when called to rule on supposedly cut-and-dry offside decisions. As soon as any sort of subjectivity is thrown into the mix, VAR is no better than a normal ref, and oftentimes worse.
